1. Background of Isaiah
 - Isaiah: Yeshayahu. Yahweh is salvation.
1장~39장 - 구약의 이야기(경고) 총 39장: Chapters 1~39 - the Old Testament story (warning), 39 chapters in all
40장~66장 - 신약의 이야기(약속) 총 27장: Chapters 40~66  - the New Testament story (promise), 27 chapters in all
이사야 1~5장 - 범죄한 예루살렘과 심판 예언: Isaiah 1~5 - sinful Jerusalem and the prophecy of judgment
<사1:1> 유다 왕 웃시야와 요담과 아하스와 히스기야 시대에 아모스의:
<Isa 1:1> The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
 - Serving through five kings, up to Manasseh, he ministered in Judah and Jerusalem, not in the northern kingdom.
 - Along with Jeremiah, he's the one who ministered the longest. A prophet ministering that long means the times were that evil. So Isaiah received this mission: 'Since it's come to this, shut the door of grace so these people can't come into God's grace – make their ears deaf, make their eyes dim, make their hearts dull, so they can't understand the truth.'
희한한 사명이죠? 보통은 선지자를 보내서 내 백성의 눈을 뜨게 하고 내:
Strange mission, right? Normally He sends a prophet to open His people's eyes and pass on His word, but to Isaiah He gives the exact opposite order. That's two hearts at once. A heart so disappointed it just wants to give up, and, even more than that, a longing that they'd still come back...
 -  Isaiah is so shocked to hear this that he asks, how long will that door of grace stay shut? And the answer is: until the people are all carried away and Jerusalem is completely empty. But He also speaks of hope – that even so, a stump will remain. We'll look at that in chapter 6.
그래서 그런지 실제로 이사야서 안에서 이사야가 누굴 전도하거나 회개케 하: Maybe that's why, inside the book of Isaiah, you don't actually see Isaiah evangelizing anyone or bringing anyone to repentance. Micah, who ministered at the same time, also just stopped at accusing the leaders and enlightening the people – it was written in a mood of hardly expecting anything from Jerusalem at that time, you know?
2. 이사야 1~5장 - 범죄한 예루살렘과 심판 예언: 2. Isaiah 1~5 - sinful Jerusalem and the prophecy of judgment
<사1:2> 하늘이여 들으라 땅이여 귀를 기울이라 여호와께서 말씀하시기를: <Isa 1:2> Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: for the LORD hath spoken, I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me. The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.
동물들도 주인을 아는데 말야. 이 범죄한 나라는 이제 망하는 것만 남았다: Even animals know their owner, you know. He says this sinful nation has nothing left but to fall. A desperate time, with barely Jerusalem alone left standing.
<사1:9> 만군의 여호와께서 우리를 위하여 조금 남겨 두지 아니하셨더면:
<Isa 1:9> Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.
 - God left a remnant because of the covenant promise He'd made to His people Israel, to Abraham and to David; if He'd simply judged them like any nation of the world, they'd have ended up like Sodom and Gomorrah.
<사1:11~13> 여호와께서 말씀하시되 너희의 무수한 제물이 내게 무엇: <Isa 1:11~13> To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the LORD: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats. Everyone, look carefully here..... God, you see.... is someone who can't stand formal, going-through-the-motions religion. The sacrifices weren't something God commanded either; they were a way of life He gave. The sacrificial system already existed. He said that if they did it, He would forgive their sins.
너희가 내 앞에 보이러 오니 그것을 누가 너희에게 요구하였느뇨: When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this at your hand
레위기에 보면 ‘드리려거든...’이라고 되어 있어요. 그런데 사람들은 그: In Leviticus it says, 'If you would offer...' But people took it as a command and thought it was something for God's sake. 'When did I ever ask you for that?'
내 마당만 밟을 뿐이니라 헛된 제물을 다시 가져오지 말라 분향은 나의 가: to tread my courts? Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; the new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, likewise: I cannot bear iniquity together with the solemn meeting.
그마나 하는 것도 형식적으로 마당만 밟는거예요. 성회와 아울러 악을 행하: And even what they do, they just tread the courtyard as a formality. I can't bear iniquity together with the solemn meeting. Holding a solemn assembly means you're at least worshiping God and trying to live a bit by His word, right? But they hold the assembly and commit evil at the same time – that's just needling God.
<사1:14~15> 내 마음이 너희의 월삭과 정한 절기를 싫어하나니 그것: <Isa 1:14~15> Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth: they are a trouble unto me; I am weary to bear them. And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.
많이 기도해도 듣지 않으신대요. 기도는 입으로 하는게 아니라 삶으로 하는: He says even if they pray a lot, He won't listen. Prayer isn't done with your mouth; it's done with your life. If your hands are full of blood – if you do evil, cheat people, speculate in houses, speculate in land, crush the poor – then no matter how much you pray, God will act like He didn't hear.
<사1:16~17> 너희는 스스로 씻으며 스스로 깨끗케 하여 내 목전에서:
<Isa 1:16~17> Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil; learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.
 - This right here is the key verse. True repentance, true godliness. God's justice is established by the people who believe in God. Judges especially have to judge rightly. Who are the oppressed? Foreign workers, temporary contract workers, store and department-store clerks who get verbally abused... There are lots of them, lots in our society too. Orphans have no power. They can't plead their own case. Widows are poor. They have no money to hire a lawyer. We have to actually help these vulnerable people in society.
<약1:27> 하나님 아버지 앞에서 정결하고 더러움이 없는 경건은 곧 고:
<Jas 1:27> Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.
 - Caring for orphans and widows, and keeping yourself from being stained by the world – that's true godliness before God..
<사1:21~23> 신실하던 성읍이 어찌하여 창기가 되었는고 공평이 거기: <Isa 1:21~23> How is the faithful city become an harlot! it was full of judgment; righteousness lodged in it; but now murderers. Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water: thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves: every one loveth gifts, and followeth after rewards: they judge not the fatherless, neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them.
정치는 높은 곳을 깎아서 낮은 곳을 메우는 것입니다. 그런데 거꾸로 하고: Politics is shaving down the high places to fill in the low places. But they're doing it backwards, right? Digging out the low places to make the high places even higher.
2장에 가면 높은 산과 높은 망대, 견고한 성벽, 아름다운 조각물들 전부:
In chapter 2 he says the high mountains and the high towers, the strong walls, the beautiful carvings – all of it is going to come crashing down. In chapter 3 it says the lower classes who were oppressed and suffered will end up ruling over the leaders. He's saying the world will be turned upside down.
 - And the reason this happens? Verse 8: For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen: because their tongue and their doings are against the LORD, to provoke the eyes of his glory
<사3:13~15> 여호와께서 변론하러 일어나시며 백성들을 심판하려고 서:
<Isa 3:13~15> The LORD standeth up to plead, and standeth to judge the people. The LORD will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses. What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith the Lord GOD of hosts.
 - Just because you've got a little something, you must not grind the faces of the poor. Real estate speculation is grinding the faces of the poor. And it's the elders and princes of the people doing all this. Members of parliament, ministers... these people make everything work in their own favor.
뿐만 아니라 우상숭배하고 있는 주제에 남자들은 교만하고 여자들은 사치했다: And not only that – while worshiping idols, the men were proud and the women were extravagant.
그것 때문에 언젠가 망할텐데 나중에 예레미야서에 가서 예루살렘이 망한 것: Because of that they'll fall someday, and later in Jeremiah, when we see Jerusalem fall, we'll see how this word came true.
<사4:1> 그 날에 일곱 여자가 한 남자를 붙잡고 말하기를 우리가 우리:
<Isa 4:1> And in that day seven women shall take hold of one man, saying, We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name, to take away our reproach.
 - This is how it expresses that the men have all died. And then it says that when God restores them, Jerusalem will actually become a hiding place.  Just like in the wilderness, when He protected and led the people with the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire...
5장에 가면 포도원의 노래가 나오는데 이스라엘 백성들을 애굽에서 옮겨다가: In chapter 5 comes the song of the vineyard: He moved the people of Israel from Egypt and planted them on the beautiful hilltop of Jerusalem, hoping for good grapes, but it bore wild grapes, He says. And in verse 13 it gives the reason the people are taken captive – in other words, the reason they lose to their enemies and are carried off as captives: they have no interest in God like this, so they are taken captive because of their lack of knowledge.
6장에 가면 이사야가 소명(부르심) 받는 장면이 나와요. 웃시야가 죽던: In chapter 6 we get the scene of Isaiah receiving his calling. Isaiah was called in the year King Uzziah died, which is around BC 740~735. Here seraphs appear – a seraph, or seraphim, is an angel. That seraph takes a live coal and touches it to Isaiah's lips and says, your sin is purged. And in verse 8, when He says, who will go for us, Isaiah says, Here am I... that's what happened.
그랬더니 하나님께서 거창한 일을 맡겨 주실 줄 알았는데 8절 보세요. 백: So he thought God would hand him some grand task, but look at verse 8. Stop up the people's ears and shut their eyes. Lest after doing all that they understand, turn back, and be healed. Can you feel God's heart right now? Isaiah cries out. Until when? Until they're completely ruined and smashed to pieces and the people are carried far away.
13절에 밤나무와 상수리 나무가 베임을 당해도 그루터기는 남아있는 것 같: In verse 13 it says that just as a chestnut tree and an oak, even when they're cut down, still leave a stump, a holy seed will remain. The chestnut tree seems to stand for the northern kingdom and the oak for the southern kingdom, and he's saying both will be cut down first. And in fact, the northern kingdom fell in B.C 721 and the southern kingdom in B.C 586.
이사야 예언자가 깨달은 것은 그 시대 이스라엘이나 남유다는 아무 희망이: What the prophet Isaiah realized was that Israel and southern Judah in that time had no hope at all, and that only when Jesus came would there be new hope. That's why Isaiah is always talking about Jesus. Looking toward the time of true restoration, it always comes back around to Jesus.
In the New Testament, whenever messianic prophecy is discussed, Isaiah is always quoted.
7장에 가면 아하스 이야기가 나오는데 열왕기하 16장 할 때 정신나간 아:
In chapter 7 comes the story of Ahaz – remember when we did 2 Kings 16 and talked about crazy Ahaz? Remember? Same time period, so it's the same story. Ahaz kept leaning on Assyria and being afraid, right? Even when he's told that within 65 years they'll fall, he doesn't believe it. So ask for a sign, then. And at the end of verse 12, he says, I will not tempt the LORD
 - Then just believe! Trembling all over and not even asking for a sign – what are you supposed to do with that? So God tells him directly. Verse 14: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel
이 말씀을 가지고 마태가 '예수님 탄생을 예언했다' 하면서 인용 했는데: Matthew quoted this passage, saying 'it prophesied the birth of Jesus', but in fact it isn't about Jesus. Since it's something the Jews knew well, he's quoting it with a stretch, using it almost like hyperbole.
여기서 처녀는 처녀가 아니고 그냥 젊은 여자 알마. 처녀는 뻬툴라. 아마: Here 'virgin' isn't 'virgin'; it's just almah, a young woman. Virgin is betulah. Probably Isaiah's wife or Ahaz's wife – anyway, some young woman King Ahaz would know well – and that woman will have a child. Name him Immanuel. Why? Because you're trembling all over. Give him a name that says God is with us.
<사7:15~16> 그가 악을 버리며 선을 택할 줄 알 때에 미쳐 버터와: <Isa 7:15~16> Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good. For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings.
The age when a child can tell good from evil is roughly 10 to 12. So in about 12 years, the two kings will be brought down. So don't be afraid.
 - Chapters 8 and 9 talk about the Messiah coming, and chapter 10 says He will judge Assyria. But before that, because God is angry, everything is going to be wiped out. Who's the tool? Assyria. So why does Assyria fall? Assyria, which was nothing but God's tool, got arrogant. Chapter 10, verses 13 and 14: For he saith, By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I am prudent: and I have removed the bounds of the people, and have robbed their treasures, and I have put down the inhabitants like a valiant man:
내 손으로 열국의 재물을 얻은 것은 새의 보금자리를 얻음 같고 온 세계를: and my hand hath found as a nest the riches of the people: and as one gathereth eggs that are left, have I gathered all the earth; and there was none that moved the wing, or opened the mouth, or peeped.
And it's because of this pride that Assyria falls.
11장에 가면 이새의 줄기에서 한 싹이 나는데 싹이 움이 되고 순이 되고: In chapter 11, a shoot comes out of the stem of Jesse – the shoot becomes a sprout, then a stalk, and when it hardens it becomes a branch, right? And bearing fruit like that, it becomes the spirit of the LORD, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD, and He judges with righteousness. That's Jesus.
Chapter 12 confesses that God, and God alone, is our salvation.
13장 부터는 열방에 대한 예언들 입니다. 주로 망한다거나 혼난다거나 하:
From chapter 13 on, it's prophecies against the nations. Mostly they're about falling or getting punished, so let's flip through them as we go.
 - Babylon (13~14), Philistia (ch. 14), Moab (ch. 15~16), Damascus (ch. 17), Cush (ch. 18), Egypt (19~20), the people of the desert of the sea (ch. 21), Dumah (ch. 21), Arabia (ch. 21), Edom (ch. 21), Babylon (ch. 21), Kedar (ch. 21), Jerusalem (ch. 22), Tyre and Sidon (ch. 23)
- God isn't just Israel's god; He's the King who rules every nation in the world, so He judges every nation in the world.
 - Other petty gods, the spirits, don't care about this stuff. At most they reign as the god of one people, and all they do is kill and destroy. But our God runs the whole world.
24장에는 종말에 일어날 일들을 말하는데 19절부터 보시면 종말 때 땅이: Chapter 24 talks about what will happen at the end; from verse 19 on, it describes the tremendous event of the earth shaking and breaking apart at the end.
그리고 25장에서는 다시 회복될 것을 이야기 하고, 모압을 벌 하실 것을: And in chapter 25 it talks again about being restored, and says He will punish Moab.
26장에서는 이스라엘에게 승리를 주실 것을 말하고, 심판과 회복을 동시에: Chapter 26 says He will give Israel victory, and speaks of judgment and restoration at the same time.  Isaiah is like this – words of judgment, restoration, and warning all mixed together. And when He speaks words of restoration, you have to pay close attention to the phrase 'in that day'. In Korean usage, when you're talking about something and say 'in that day', it means the day you were just talking about, right? But Hebrew usage isn't like that. It doesn't mean the day you were just talking about; it means 'a certain day God has set'. Mostly it refers to when Jesus comes again.
<사27:1> 그 날에 여호와께서 그 견고하고 크고 강한 칼로 날랜 뱀:
<Isa 27:1> In that day the LORD with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.
 - Rev 12:9 the great dragon = the old serpent = the devil = Satan. He kills the serpent. It even talks about killing the dragon at the end. (Rev 20)
 - Chapter 28 is a warning to the corrupt leaders of Ephraim
 - Chapter 29: Woe to Ariel. Ariel is a nickname for Jerusalem. Something astonishing will happen – He'll make them unable to understand God's word. That's Isaiah's calling too.  It says they honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.
 - In chapter 30 He warns the people who lean on Egypt and Assyria. Look from verse 9
<사30:9~11> 대저 이는 패역한 백성이요 거짓말 하는 자식이요 여호:
<Isa 30:9~11> That this is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of the LORD: which say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits: get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us.
 - They hate hearing the law of the LORD, they're annoyed by the seers' prophecies, they threaten the preachers to make the sermons a little softer, and in the end they say, make God go away. They even say rude things like that. It's the same today. Not many people like hearing the word.  Sermons keep getting shorter. The Puritans preached two or three hours at a time... Our Hangiseon is doing well, right? We do 14 hours at a time.
 - Chapter 31 says woe to those who go down to Egypt for help.
 - Chapter 32 says a king will reign in righteousness. Near term, Josiah; far off, Jesus.
 - Chapter 33 says the Lord will surely rise up. When the Lord rises up and judges, what kind of person can stand at the end?
<사33:15~16> 오직 의롭게 행하는 자, 정직히 말하는자, 토색한:
<Isa 33:15~16> He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, that shaketh his hands from holding of bribes, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil; he shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks: bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure.
 - Chapter 34 talks about the destruction of Edom; we'll look at it together when we do Obadiah
 - Chapter 35 sings that even so, someday there will be restoration.
36~39장 까지는 히스기야 왕의 공과 과, 잘한 것과 잘못 한 것을 이: Chapters 36~39 talk about King Hezekiah's merits and faults, what he did right and what he did wrong; it's the same as 2 Kings 18~20. We'll look at it when we get there.
이제 40장부터는 전혀 다른 분위기로 바뀝니다. 제 2 이사야라고 하기도: Now from chapter 40 the mood changes completely. Some even call it Second Isaiah.  It's talking about going home, around the time the Babylonian Exile is almost over.
이전 내용과는 다르게 힘이 넘치고 위로가 있고 소망이 넘치는 그런 분위기: Unlike what came before, the mood is full of strength, full of comfort, overflowing with hope. So if you put this alongside the latter part of Daniel, the historical flow is similar and it just makes sense; we only read it here because Isaiah is one book. They're stories from the same period.
<사40:1~2> 너희 하나님이 가라사대 너희는 위로하라 내 백성을 위로:
<Isa 40:1~2> Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God. Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD's hand double for all her sins.
 - It says the time of 70 years' hard service is now over, and it's time to be comforted. These are words the Isaiah who wrote the earlier part couldn't have written.
<사41:8~10> 그러나 나의 종 너 이스라엘아 나의 택한 야곱아 나의:
<Isa 41:8~10> But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend. Thou whom I have taken from the ends of the earth, and called thee from the chief men thereof, and said unto thee, Thou art my servant; I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away. Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
 - People misunderstand this part a lot too – it's not said to us. But some folks made it into a song, so it's a well-known verse. This verse is addressed to the people of Israel who served out their 70 years in Babylon well and whose time of service was over.
<사42:1~4> 내가 붙드는 나의 종, 내 마음에 기뻐하는 나의 택한:
<Isa 42:1~4> Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles. He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street. A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth. He shall not fail nor be discouraged, till he have set judgment in the earth: and the isles shall wait for his law.
 - The picture of God's servant. Near term it points to the prophet speaking these words himself, and far off it shows us Jesus. From verse 5 on, He doesn't do all this just so Israel alone can eat well and live well; they'll become a light to the Gentiles and bring salvation to everyone in the world.
<사43:10> 나 여호와가 말하노라 너희는 나의 증인, 나의 종으로 택:
<Isa 43:10> Ye are my witnesses, saith the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen: that ye may know and believe me, and understand that I am he: before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.
 - Once again He reconfirms Israel's mission as a nation. That is, to be God's witnesses. If there was no god before God, and there's none after Him either, then God alone is God, right?
<사43:11~12> 나 곧 나는 여호와라 나 외에 구원자가 없느니라 내:
<Isa 43:11~12> I, even I, am the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour. I have declared, and have saved, and I have shewed, when there was no strange god among you: therefore ye are my witnesses, saith the LORD, that I am God.
 - This is exactly Isaiah – Yeshayahu – the LORD is the One who saves.
44장 부터는 우상숭배의 가련한 상황을 이야기 하는데 사람들 눈에 뭔가가:
From chapter 44 it talks about the pitiful state of idol worship: something covers people's eyes, they can't see, and they become foolish. So they can't even say, 'Isn't this thing in my right hand a lie through and through?' and they go on worshiping idols.
 - Chapter 45 is the story of Cyrus, the anointed. God anoints and uses even a Gentile. We'll talk about this in more detail in the Intertestamental Period, but Cyrus was someone who hadn't even been born yet. And yet it says He will set Israel free through that man.
 - Chapter 46: the gods of Babylon will surely collapse. Bel was the highest god of Babylon.
 - Chapter 47: Babylon too will be brought down when its time comes.
 - Chapter 48: I will show you hidden, secret things. That is, the people of Israel will go home, and Babylon will fall.
 - Chapter 49: the mission of the servant of the LORD. That is, to be made a light to the Gentiles, carrying salvation to the ends of the earth.
 - Chapter 50: the Lord will never abandon His own people.
 - Chapter 51: so, My people, pay attention to Me.
52장은 70년동안 잠들어 있던 시온을 깨우는 이야기. 70년 복역의 때: Chapter 52 is about waking Zion, which had been asleep for 70 years. The 70 years of service are complete, so He's crying out, now get up!
53장에 보면 예수님의 외모가 아름답지 않았다는 말을 하는데 고운 모양도:
Chapter 53 says Jesus' appearance wasn't beautiful – no form or comeliness. Didn't He come looking like this on purpose? So the hotshots wouldn't meet Jesus. Anyway, it prophesies that this Messiah will suffer. There He grabs onto Jesus again, right? Isaiah wasn't called to wake the people up with these words of revelation; he was called NOT to tell them these things, because they needed a good lesson.
 - Chapter 54: don't be afraid. Jesus will come as the Savior of the people. So until then, the people won't be completely wiped out; their line will be kept alive.
그러니까 이런거 저런거 두려워하지 말고 나만 의지해라. 하면서 소싯적에: So don't be afraid of this or that, just rely on Me. And with that comes the story of Hephzibah, Hezekiah's wife, who was rejected when she was young. We don't know it well, but for the people of Israel it was a story still vivid in memory.
히스기야의 아내 중 헵시바란 여자가 있었는데 젊었을 때에 버림 받았다가: Among Hezekiah's wives was a woman named Hephzibah, and just as she was rejected when she was young and then taken back again, it's a picture that says: I rejected the Jews of Jerusalem, but I'll take them back again.
<55:1~2> 너희 목마른 자들아 물로 나아오라 돈 없는 자도 오라 너:
<55:1~2> Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price. Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness.
 - Don't wear yourself out over things that aren't bread; if you just listen to God, joy comes.
 - Chapter 56: practice justice
 - Chapter 57: the righteous live even when they die. The wicked are dead even while they live.
 - Chapter 58: teaching on fasting.
6.나의 기뻐하는 금식은 흉악의 결박을 풀어 주며 멍에의 줄을 끌러 주며:
6. Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke? Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?
 - It's not that God delights in fasting. People think God is pleased when they fast, without even reading what comes before and after, but that's not it. People were fasting while having fun and doing all kinds of business and fighting – what kind of fast is that? He doesn't delight in that kind of fast; He delights in the kind of fast in verses 6~7. It's saying, if you're going to fast, do it right – not that He delights in fasting.
금식은 한 마디로 단식 투쟁이예요. 무슨 거룩하고, 경건하고 그런게 아니:
In a word, fasting is a hunger strike. It's not something holy or pious. God wants us to eat well and do God's work in good health. Nowhere in the Bible does God command fasting. People get desperate, so they stop eating and drinking and cling to God. He has never recognized fasting as a means of godliness. On the contrary, there are countless places where He points out that kind of detestable behavior.
 - Chapter 59 is what they realized in Babylon - the people admit the prophet's cries pointing out their sins, and they confess
 - In chapter 60 He encourages them to arise and shine. In My wrath I struck you before, but now in My favor I have had mercy on you.
 - Chapter 61 speaks of the beautiful news of salvation. Later, in the synagogue in Nazareth of Galilee, Jesus reads this passage and says, today this word is fulfilled in your hearing.
 - Chapter 62: prepare the way for the people – it's about the time having come to return from Babylon
 - Chapter 63: God will judge Edom terribly.
 - Chapter 64: the servant's prayer - we did wrong, so please forgive us.
 - Chapters 65~66: the story of the new heaven and the new earth. Isaiah is also called the Bible in miniature. Revelation has the new heaven and the new earth.
 - Chapter 66, verse 2
나 여호와가 말하노라 나의 손이 이 모든 것을 지어서 다 이루었느니라 무: For all those things hath mine hand made, and all those things have been, saith the LORD: but to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word.
회복의 때라고 해서 아무나 다 되는 것이 아니라 마음이 가난하고 심령이: Just because it's the time of restoration doesn't mean it's for just anyone; it's the one who is poor in heart, contrite in spirit, and knows how to tremble at God's word who will be looked upon.
All right, Isaiah is a long book – 66 chapters – and we've looked at it in summary.
